html:
The Mosquito Coast is the Caribbean shore of eastern Nicaragua and Honduras, named after the Miskito people. From the 1600s to 1894 it was the Miskito Kingdom, under British protection. The map shows it in 1715.

The Miskito people took in African survivors of shipwrecks and escaped slaves and grew strong through trade with English buccaneers and settlers. With English guns they raided Spanish towns and native peoples across Central America, taking captives to sell. Their kings were crowned with English support, and Britain kept small settlements on the coast.

Spain never controlled the shore. After independence, Nicaragua and Honduras claimed it, and in 1860 Britain gave up its protection and the coast became the Mosquito Reserve inside Nicaragua. In 1894 Nicaragua took it over by force. It remains a separate world, with Miskito, Creole and Garífuna people and English widely spoken.
